transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I came in because... things have really fallen apart for me lately. Ever since my wife had a fall, I've gone from being the man with all the lists and the plan, to just... sitting at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. 

I find myself crying, or snapping over absolutely nothing at all. And everything else is just piling up—the bills, my mentoring calls, even basic housework. It's like I just can't make myself function anymore.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things that you usually find pleasurable, like hobbies, socializing, or other activities?

I don't really know. I haven't even tried to do any of my usual hobbies or see anyone. I'm just... I'm so focused on the medication chart and the house falling apart that I haven't even thought about doing anything for fun. So I couldn't tell you if I'd enjoy it or not.
Do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I don't think I'd say I feel depressed most of the day. I mean, I definitely have those moments where I just break down and cry, like I mentioned. But the rest of the time, it's not really a constant sadness. It's more that I just feel completely overwhelmed and stressed by everything I'm supposed to be handling right now.
Can you think of a time recently when you weren’t feeling overwhelmed—maybe a quiet moment—where you felt any interest or desire to engage in activities you used to enjoy?

No, I... I really can't think of a time like that. Even when things are quiet in the house—like if my wife is resting—my mind doesn't go to my old interests. I'm usually just sitting there worrying about the next medication dose, or thinking about how far behind I am on everything else. 

I haven't felt any desire to pick up a hobby or do anything I used to enjoy. The pressure of it all just doesn't really go away, even in the quiet moments.
Before your wife's fall, had you been feeling down, losing interest in things, or struggling with low mood even when there wasn't an obvious reason to feel overwhelmed?

No, not at all. Before her fall, things were... they were fine. We had our routine, I had my interests. I wasn't feeling down or anything like that. Her fall was only about two months ago, and this—me feeling this overwhelmed and stressed out—that only started after I had to take over all the caregiving. It wasn't an issue before that.
Have you found yourself getting easily irritated or angry lately, even over small things?

Yes, I have. I've been snapping over absolutely nothing. That's actually a big part of why I came in. 

Since my wife's fall, I've gone from being the man with the lists and the plan to... well, just sitting at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. I'll end up crying or just getting angry over the smallest things. And I'm letting everything else slide. Bills, my old mentoring calls, even basic housework—it's all just piling up. It's like I just can't make myself function anymore.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't really use the word hopeless. And it's not... it's not this constant feeling of being down all day, every day. 

It's more just this massive weight of being overwhelmed. Like I mentioned, I'll sit there and get frustrated or cry because the pressure is just too much, but I don't think it's hopelessness. It's just the sheer stress of trying to keep up with it all and feeling like I can't.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even when you’ve had the chance to do them?

No, it's not that I've lost interest, really. It's more that... I just don't have the time or energy for them right now. Like the mentoring calls I mentioned, I still care about doing them, but with everything going on with my wife's care, I just can't bring myself to focus on them. If I had the time and wasn't so completely drained by all this stress, I'd still want to do the things I used to enjoy. It's just the situation that's stopping me, not a lack of interest.
Have you had any two-week period since your wife’s fall where you felt down, lost interest in things, or experienced other symptoms nearly every day?

No, not for a solid two-week stretch, no. Like I said, I'm not feeling down or hopeless all the time, and I haven't lost interest in things. It's just the stress and the crying when it all gets to be too much. But it's not an everyday, all-day kind of thing for two weeks straight.
Since your wife's fall, have you had any days where you felt no interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even for a little while?

No, not really. Like I was saying before, the interest is still there. If I had a free afternoon and wasn't completely exhausted from managing the house and her appointments, I'd gladly go do something I enjoy. It's just that I don't have the capacity for it right now. So, no, I haven't had days where the actual interest or pleasure is gone.
Since your wife's fall, have you had any days where you felt absolutely no interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even for a short time?
No, I haven't. I know we just went over this, but it really hasn't changed. The interest hasn't disappeared. I just... I don't have the time or the energy to do anything right now.
Since your wife's fall, have you had several days in a row where you felt down or had no interest in doing anything, even for a few hours each day?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I feel like we're going in circles here a bit. I haven't had days where I'm just sitting around feeling down or completely uninterested in things. It's just the overwhelming stress of the situation, you know? The interest is there, I'm just stretched too thin to act on it.
Since your wife's fall, have you had several days where, for most of the day, you felt down or had no interest in doing anything at all, even things you used to enjoy?

Doctor, I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again. No, I haven't. I really don't have days where I just feel down or lose interest in everything for most of the day. 

It's exactly what I said before—the interest is completely intact. I'm just incredibly overwhelmed with taking care of my wife and managing the house by myself. That's what is keeping me from doing things, not a lack of interest.

Can you recall any specific instance since your wife's fall where you tried to engage in one of your usual hobbies or activities you used to enjoy, but found absolutely no interest or pleasure in it at all?

No, I can't. Like I've been saying, it's not that I try to do my hobbies and don't enjoy them... I just haven't tried. I don't have the time to even attempt to do anything for myself right now. If I had a spare hour, I'm sure I'd enjoy reading or working in the garage just as much as I always have. It's just... there are no spare hours anymore.
Since your wife's fall, have you had several days where, for most of the day, you felt down or had no interest in doing anything at all, even things you used to enjoy?

Doctor, you literally just asked me that exact same question. I don't know how else to say it. No, I haven't. I'm not depressed, I'm not sitting around feeling down or losing interest in my life. I'm just completely buried under all the work and the stress of taking care of my wife right now.

Looking back further than the time since your wife's fall—say, in the year before that—did you ever have a period of two weeks or longer where you felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even if it wasn't connected to any specific stressor?

No, nothing like that. Before her fall... things were perfectly fine. We had a good routine going. I never had any weeks where I felt down or, you know, stopped caring about my hobbies. Life was just normal up until she got hurt.
